project.project_description: The Mida Creek Mangrove Restoration Project restores and protects approximately 1,200 hectares of degraded mangrove ecosystems along the Kenyan coast. Activities include active replanting of native mangrove species, removal of invasive vegetation, and community-based monitoring. The project generates carbon credits through sequestration and avoidance of further degradation, while delivering co-benefits including biodiversity habitat, coastal protection, and livelihood support for local fishing communities.
project.community_frameworks: Free, prior, and informed consent (FPIC) obtained from Giriama and Digo communities. Grievance redress mechanism established. Benefit-sharing agreement signed with three local cooperatives covering 640 community members.
project.project_governance_structure: Project governed by a joint steering committee comprising Blue Carbon Kenya Ltd, two elected community representatives, and the Kenya Forest Service. Decisions require 75% approval. Annual external audit of governance processes.
project.public_comment_summary: 30-day public comment period held November 2022. Fifteen submissions received; key concerns related to fishing access rights and benefit distribution were addressed in the revised project design document.

organization.organization_mission: To restore and protect coastal blue carbon ecosystems across East Africa, delivering verified carbon credits alongside biodiversity and livelihood co-benefits.
organization.organization_team_experience: Leadership team combines 20+ years of blue carbon science, MRV, and community development. Previously developed three certified mangrove projects in Mozambique and Tanzania totaling 3,800 ha.

validation.validation_report_summary: SCS Global Services (VVB-SCS-0021) validated the Mida Creek Mangrove Restoration Project against VCS v4.5 and methodology VM0033 v2.1. The validation confirmed the project boundary of approximately 1,200 hectares, the additionality demonstration, the baseline scenario, and the monitoring plan. Four findings were raised during the desk review and site audit, all of which were resolved before the final validation report was issued. The validation team concluded that the project design conforms to the applied standard and methodology.
validation.validation_stage_description: Desk review of the project design document and supporting evidence, followed by a site audit at Mida Creek with community and project team interviews, a 30-day public comment period hosted on the registry, resolution of four findings raised by the validation team, and issuance of the final validation report.

status.validation_status_reason: Four findings raised during the desk review and site audit were addressed by the project developer and closed by the validation team in April 2023.
Final validation report issued on 2023-05-10. The validation is valid until 2028-05-10, after which the project must be revalidated to maintain its registry standing.

cobenefit_target.overview_of_the_projects_impact: Restore degraded intertidal habitat with native mangrove species, improve habitat connectivity, and increase nursery habitat available to fish, crustaceans, birds, and other coastal wildlife.
cobenefit_target.overview_of_the_projects_approach_to_ tr: Map the restoration boundary annually using satellite imagery and field-verified GIS surveys. Permanent sample plots are assessed twice each year for planted area, species composition, stem density, and seedling survival.
cobenefit_target.unit_description: Area of degraded mangrove habitat restored and maintained under active project management
cobenefit_target.baseline_value: 0 hectares under project-led restoration at the project start date
cobenefit_target.target_value: 1,200 hectares restored and maintained by the end of project year 10

cobenefit_target.overview_of_the_projects_impact: Increase natural shoreline protection by restoring mangrove belts that reduce wave energy, stabilize sediments, and lower erosion exposure for nearby settlements and community infrastructure.
cobenefit_target.overview_of_the_projects_approach_to_ tr: Establish fixed shoreline transects and erosion pins, combine field measurements with drone imagery, and confirm protected shoreline segments through annual community hazard-mapping exercises.
cobenefit_target.unit_description: Length of shoreline with restored mangrove cover providing enhanced natural protection
cobenefit_target.baseline_value: 0 km classified as enhanced by project intervention
cobenefit_target.target_value: 18 km of shoreline with enhanced mangrove-based protection by project year 10

cobenefit_target.overview_of_the_projects_impact: Create paid local employment and contracting opportunities in nursery operations, planting, monitoring, patrols, data collection, and restoration-linked enterprises, with priority for participating coastal communities.
cobenefit_target.overview_of_the_projects_approach_to_ tr: Maintain payroll and contractor records, verify residence through cooperative membership records, remove duplicate individuals, and reconcile the total during each annual social monitoring cycle.
cobenefit_target.unit_description: Number of local residents receiving paid project employment or project-funded contracts during a reporting year
cobenefit_target.baseline_value: 0 local residents receiving project-funded employment before implementation
cobenefit_target.target_value: At least 180 unique local residents receiving paid work or contracts annually by project year 5

cobenefit_target.overview_of_the_projects_impact: Increase women's participation in paid restoration, nursery, monitoring, cooperative leadership, and technical roles while applying equal-pay and safe-workplace requirements.
cobenefit_target.overview_of_the_projects_approach_to_ tr: Track sex-disaggregated payroll and contractor records, review role categories and pay bands each quarter, and validate results through confidential worker interviews and cooperative records.
cobenefit_target.unit_description: Change in the share of paid project roles held by women compared with the baseline share
cobenefit_target.baseline_value: 22% of comparable paid conservation roles held by women in the baseline survey
cobenefit_target.target_value: +23 percentage points, equivalent to women holding at least 45% of paid project roles by project year 5

cobenefit_target.overview_of_the_projects_impact: Distribute restoration-linked benefits through local cooperatives and community institutions, supporting household priorities, small-enterprise development, training, and transparent participation in project decisions.
cobenefit_target.overview_of_the_projects_approach_to_ tr: Reconcile benefit-payment registers, training attendance, cooperative membership records, and grievance logs. Community representatives review and sign off the consolidated beneficiary list each year.
cobenefit_target.unit_description: Number of unique community members receiving a documented monetary or in-kind project benefit during the reporting year
cobenefit_target.baseline_value: 0 community members receiving project-generated benefits before implementation
cobenefit_target.target_value: 640 unique community members receiving documented benefits annually by project year 5

cobenefit_impact.achieved_project_impact: By the end of the hypothetical 2024 monitoring period, 425 hectares of degraded mangrove habitat had been replanted or placed under assisted natural regeneration and active community monitoring.
Field and drone surveys identified 7.5 km of shoreline where restored mangrove belts met the project's minimum width, vegetation density, and continuity criteria for enhanced natural protection.
During the hypothetical 2024 reporting year, 136 unique local residents received paid work or project-funded contracts across nursery, planting, patrol, monitoring, and data-collection activities.
Women held 41% of paid project roles during the hypothetical 2024 reporting year, compared with a 22% baseline share.
cobenefit_impact.achieved_value: +19 percentage points, equivalent to 41% of paid roles

cobenefit_impact.achieved_project_impact: A reconciled beneficiary register recorded 512 unique community members receiving cooperative distributions, paid training, livelihood inputs, or other documented project-funded benefits during the hypothetical 2024 reporting year.

agreement.agreement_notes: Illustrative forward-purchase arrangement for the Mida Creek Mangrove Restoration Project. The buyer prepays 40% of the committed amount, with the balance paid in three 20% tranches after verified issuance and registry transfer for the 2026, 2027, and 2028 vintages. Deliveries are capped at 50,000 tCO2e per eligible vintage and remain subject to methodology compliance, buffer deductions, no-double-counting checks, insurance conditions, and the project community benefit-sharing obligations. All counterparty, insurer, policy, price, volume, date, cost, revenue, and funding details in this record are hypothetical.

offtake.offtake_agreement_credit_requirements: Verified Carbon Units representing tCO2e removals from the Mida Creek project; eligible vintages 2026-2028; issued under the Verra VCS using VM0033 version 2.1; verified by an approved validation/verification body; net of applicable buffer contributions; free of prior retirement, cancellation, encumbrance, or double counting; and supported by registry transfer evidence.

details.verification_description: First periodic verification of the Mida Creek Mangrove Restoration Project, covering the 2023 monitoring period. SCS Global Services conducted a site audit at Mida Creek from 2024-02-05 to 2024-02-12, led by Grace Wanjiku as lead verifier, and reviewed the monitoring report, plot-level biomass measurements from 42 permanent sample plots, soil organic carbon sampling, and remote sensing evidence of canopy cover change. Net verified removals of 52,300 tCO2e were confirmed from 66,200 tCO2e of gross monitored removals, after a 5% uncertainty deduction of 3,310 tCO2e, a leakage deduction of 1,150 tCO2e, and a buffer pool contribution of 9,440 tCO2e. The verified quantity corresponds to issuance batch cdop:KEN:VCS-4721:B1, and the buffer pool contribution forms part of the 18,900 tCO2e of cumulative buffer pool deposits recorded in the project durability record. One Forward Action Request was raised regarding documentation of plot re-measurement intervals, to be closed at the next verification. All quantities, identifiers, signature payloads, and dates in this record are hypothetical.

deductions.verification_leakage_risk_mitigation_str: Activity-shifting leakage is monitored across a 5 km belt surrounding the project area using annual high-resolution imagery and household fuelwood surveys. Alternative fuelwood woodlots and improved cookstoves were provided to the three adjacent communities to reduce displacement of harvesting pressure. See section 6.4 of the monitoring report: https://registry.verra.org/app/projectDetail/VCS/4721/monitoring

vvb.accreditation: Accredited to ISO 14065 by the ANSI National Accreditation Board (ANAB); approved by Verra as a validation and verification body for the AFOLU sectoral scope under VCS v4.5.
vvb.name: SCS Global Services
vvb.selection: Selected by the project developer through a competitive tender open to Verra-approved validation and verification bodies with AFOLU sectoral scope accreditation and prior blue carbon experience in East Africa. Three bodies were invited, two submitted proposals, and the award was made on technical capability and demonstrated tidal wetland experience rather than on price alone. The same body was retained for periodic verification, with a separate audit team to preserve independence between the validation and verification engagements.
